newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds restrained,end little changed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds restrained,end little changed.

text.p: *Australian bonds were restrained to a narrow range, finishing little changed from Tuesday's closing levels.
*Treasury offering A$100 million of 2020 indexed bonds Thursday.

Australian bonds were restrained to a narrow range, finishing little changed from Tuesday's closing levels in the absence of major data to suggest whether or not a further easing in monetary policy was possible.

The market will have to wait until Monday's third quarter capital expediture report, which includes business investment expectations, before such speculation can release the market from it current straitjacket, traders said.
In the meantime, long-dated yields are seen restricted on the downside to 7.0 percent, while retracements are also seen limited given recent solid rebounds on corrective moves.
"The market's stuck with nothing to go on in the short-term. It drifted off a bit this afternoon, but the turnover has been pretty awful," one trader added.
Westpac Banking Corp said its September leading index fell 0.3 percent, its coincident index 2.2 percent and leading index of inflation by 0.1 of a percentage point.

Bill Evans, Westpac's General Manager, Economics said the further fall in the inflation index continued to suggest further alleviation of inflationary pressures. "Combined with a stagnant leading index of activity and weakening coincident index, another cut in interest rates should be a high priority."

The local market underperformed U.S. Treasuries, which continued Tuesday's bid tone following further soft economic data in Tokyo trading. The U.S. faces a US$12.5 billion five-year note auction later today, along with international trade data for September.
The 10-year bond contract found support on a move towards 92.860 after failing to breach resistance at 92.920. The contract made a solid rebound from 92.805 on Tuesday.
